steps.title: The glue word: JOIN
steps.prompt:
Products only have a category NUMBER (category_id) - the name lives in another table.
JOIN glues two tables side by side by matching keys, like puzzle pieces.
ON p.category_id = c.id is the instruction: 'glue where the product's category number matches the category's own number.'
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id;
hints: Short names p and c are nicknames for the tables.
ON tells SQL which columns to match.
Products carry category_id; categories carry id.
Type the JOIN with ON p.category_id = c.id.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id;
steps.memory_trick: JOIN = glue; ON = where to glue.

steps.title: Fill the ON
steps.prompt:
The glue needs its matching instruction. Fill the blank:
SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON ___.category_id = ___.id;
steps.task: Fill both blanks with the table nicknames.
hints: The nicknames are p and c.
The first condition is about products.
Product's column is category_id; the category's is id.
Fill with p then c.
steps.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id;
steps.seed_sql: SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON ___.category_id = ___.id;

steps.title: Sales need names
steps.prompt:
Invoices record customer NUMBERS, not names. JOIN brings the names in:
SELECT s.id, c.name FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id;
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT s.id, c.name FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id;
hints: Nickname sales as s and customers as c.
ON matches customer_id to id.
Show the sale id and the customer's name.
Type: SELECT s.id, c.name FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT s.id, c.name FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id;
steps.memory_trick: Keys in one table become names when you JOIN.

steps.title: Predict the row count
steps.prompt:
There are 45 sales and 30 customers. JOIN matches every sale to one customer.
SELECT count(*) FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id;
steps.task: How many rows does the join return?
hints: Each sale glues to exactly one customer.
There are 45 sales.
No sale is left behind in an inner join.
Answer: 45.
steps.memory_trick: INNER JOIN keeps only rows that find a partner.

steps.title: Products with real category names
steps.prompt: Final puzzle piece - switch the numbers for names on the full products list:
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id;
hints: Join products p to categories c.
ON p.category_id = c.id.
Show p.name and c.name.
Write: SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, c.name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id;
steps.memory_trick: From now on, JOIN is your everyday friend.
